q: The ripple tank is a convenient piece of apparatus for demonstrating the properties of _____.
e: The ripple tank is a convenient piece of apparatus for demonstrating the properties of waves. The physics in this sentence is built around waves.

q: The surface that joins all the points of the same phase is called a _____.
e: The surface that joins all the points of the same phase is called a wavefront. Wavefront names the surface that joins all the points of the same phase. Wavelength: the distance from one crest to the next crest.

q: The turning back of waves when they strike an obstacle is called the _____ of waves.
e: The turning back of waves when they strike an obstacle is called the reflection of waves. Reflection here means light bouncing back from a surface. Refraction: light bending as it changes medium.

q: When waves strike a straight barrier, the angle of incidence is _____ to the angle of reflection.
e: When waves strike a straight barrier, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. The physics in this sentence is built around equal.

q: In the reflection of waves, the wavelength and velocity of the wave remain _____.
e: In the reflection of waves, the wavelength and velocity of the wave remain constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: When plane waves strike a concave barrier, the reflected waves _____.
e: When plane waves strike a concave barrier, the reflected waves converge. The physics in this sentence is built around converge.

q: When plane waves strike a convex barrier, the reflected waves _____.
e: When plane waves strike a convex barrier, the reflected waves diverge. The physics in this sentence is built around diverge.

q: The speed of water waves depends on the _____ of water.
e: The speed of water waves depends on the depth of water. The physics in this sentence is built around depth. Temperature: how hot or cold a body is.

q: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water, the velocity of the wave is _____ and the wavelength is shorter.
e: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water, the velocity of the wave is lesser and the wavelength is shorter. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: A change in direction of waves when they are incident to the boundary with an angle is called _____.
e: A change in direction of waves when they are incident to the boundary with an angle is called refraction. Refraction here means light bending as it changes medium. Reflection: light bouncing back from a surface.

q: In refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but the _____ remains the same.
e: In refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but the frequency remains the same. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Speed: how fast the path length changes, with no direction.

q: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap or around an _____.
e: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap or around an obstacle. The physics in this sentence is built around obstacle.

q: In the diffraction of water waves, the wider the gap, the _____ the waves spread out.
e: In the diffraction of water waves, the wider the gap, the less the waves spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around less.

q: In the diffraction of water waves, the narrower the gap, the _____ the waves spread out.
e: In the diffraction of water waves, the narrower the gap, the more the waves spread out. The physics in this sentence is built around more.

q: In diffraction, the wavelength of the wave does not _____.
e: In diffraction, the wavelength of the wave does not change. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.
